name: BP-CC1407P-9-FE BoosterPack plug-in module
sources: EVM user guide SWRU633 (September 2026, Figure 2-1 board drawing, Table 2-1 header signals, section 2.5 LEDs, BOM); CC1407P data sheet SWRS301 (September 2026, ADVANCE INFORMATION, sections 6.4, 6.5, 6.17); both read 2026-10-07

columns.head: The chip: CC1407P
items: Radios: sub-1 GHz transceiver
Sends and receives only. It runs no program of yours: a host LaunchPad kit drives it over SPI
Speed: 0.75 kbps to 2.4 Mbps
Slow modes reach farthest (-131 dBm), fast OFDM modes carry more data
Power: up to +22 dBm out
134 mA while sending at full power, 6.9 mA listening, 0.8 uA in standby
Limit: 902 to 928 MHz on this board
A SAW filter in the receive path fixes the band to the US 915 MHz band

columns.head: Connections to the host
items: Clock, data in, data out, chip select, up to 12 MHz
GPIO: pin 23 INT, pin 36 RESET
INT says 'I have data'; the host also watches pin 14 for 'ready'
Debug link: 20-pin edge connector
For an LP-XDS110 or LP-XDS110ET probe and SmartRF Studio 8 (Windows only)
Software
TI's TRX plug-in (F2 SDK hosts) or TI's Zephyr shield; both preview quality

columns.head: On the board, and missing
items: On the board
SMA antenna socket, red and green LEDs on jumper P2, 48 MHz crystal, RF switch
Headers
40-pin BoosterPack connectors J1 and J2, male and female, so it stacks
Not fitted
No antenna is listed in the kit or the parts list: bring a 915 MHz SMA antenna
Watch out
Preview part: prototype board in limited quantity, and the setup API changes at release
